encoder_boundary_note: os.path.isfile is a filesystem probe, NOT in the harvested op-surface (boolean/compare/arith/bit/unary/conditional mirrored from Configuration.py ExpressionEvaluator). Its truth depends on (string path value, live filesystem state), so it is modeled only as an uninterpreted Bool isfile=Bool('os_path_isfile_cachePath'); the branch predicate is Not(isfile). Under that encoding Z3 reports both polarities sat trivially because the seeded cachePath domain ('__nonexistent__'/'__existing_regular_file__') is a placeholder pair, not a constraint the solver can relate to the probe result. The two domain tokens are exactly the two filesystem preconditions, not two distinct string values that determine the outcome.

true_examples.precondition: no regular file at cachePath (file absent, or path is a directory / dangling symlink). Domain token __nonexistent__. This is the cache-miss path: _readCacheIfValid returns None and the caller proceeds to (re)build the benchmark step.

false_examples.precondition: a regular file exists at cachePath. Domain token __existing_regular_file__. This is the cache-hit path: control falls through to LibraryIO.read(cachePath) and content validation (_cacheDataMatches).

z3_model.encoding: isfile = Bool('os_path_isfile_cachePath'); pred = Not(isfile); uninterpreted external predicate

empirical_confirmation.method: in-container python: same cachePath string, probed before and after creating the file

directory_arg.note: isfile is False for a directory, so a dir at cachePath also takes the True (cache-miss) branch

empirical_confirmation.conclusion: Identical input string value yields opposite predicate results depending solely on live filesystem state -> runtime-dependent, not statically decidable from the seeded string domain.

notes: Guard-return at the top of _readCacheIfValid. Predicate is the cache-miss guard: True iff no regular file exists at cachePath, in which case the function returns None before any LibraryIO.read / YAML parse / _cacheDataMatches validation. cachePath is caller-derived: _loadCacheIfMatches passes os.path.join(cacheDir,'cache.yaml') (cacheDir = stepBaseDir/caches/<sha256[:12] cacheKey>); _loadLegacyCacheIfMatches passes os.path.join(stepBaseDir,'cache.yaml'). All upstream path components are deterministic given public inputs (OutputPath CLI + BenchmarkProblems YAML), but the leaf predicate itself is a pure os.path.isfile filesystem probe and therefore runtime-dependent. Witnesses are by VALUE (not solver-proven): TRUE = no file at cachePath (cache miss); FALSE = a regular file at cachePath (cache hit). To pin TRUE downstream: call with a cachePath that does not point at a regular file -> returns None. To pin FALSE: create a regular file at cachePath -> control proceeds to LibraryIO.read. Z3 4.16.0 was actually run in-container; the uninterpreted-Bool model is the maximal sound encoding given the op-surface boundary (os.path.isfile is outside it). Mirrors sibling e278ed04... (os.path.exists assert in ClientWriter.py).
